en: open a port or airport; open a port to foreigners

examples.en: The new airport opens next month.

examples.ko: 그 항구는 백 년 전에 개항했어요.
examples.en: That port was opened a hundred years ago.

examples.ko: 공항을 개항하려면 아직 공사가 더 필요해요.
examples.en: To open the airport, more construction is still needed.

examples.ko: 개항한 지 얼마 안 돼서 이용객이 적어요.
examples.en: It hasn't been long since it opened, so there are few users.

examples.ko: 언제 개항하는지 알면 표를 미리 사 둘게요.
examples.en: If I find out when it opens, I'll buy tickets in advance.
As soon as the airport opened, crowds of visitors came.

explain: 항구뿐 아니라 공항에도 써요. 주어는 사람이 아니라 보통 공항이나 항구예요. 문을 닫는 쪽은 '폐쇄하다'처럼 다른 말을 써요.
explain_en: It is used for airports as well as ports. The subject is usually an airport or port, not a person. For closing, a different word such as '폐쇄하다' is used.

examples.en: There is a small church at the end of the village.
I attend worship at the church every Sunday.

examples.ko: 새 교회당은 건물이 정말 높고 아름다워요.
examples.en: The new church building is really tall and beautiful.
I hear the bell of the old church every morning.
It started raining, so everyone went into the church.

examples.ko: 교회당 건물을 새로 짓는 데 삼 년이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took three years to build the new church building.

explain: '교회'는 모임과 건물을 다 가리키고, '교회당'은 예배드리는 건물 자체를 말할 때 써요. 천주교의 건물은 '성당'이라고 해요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '교회'라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: '교회' can mean both the congregation and the building, while '교회당' points to the building itself. A Catholic church building is called '성당'. In daily talk people often just say '교회'.

examples.ko: 버스가 끼익 하고 섰을 때 심장이 멎는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: When the bus stopped with a screech, I thought my heart would stop.

examples.ko: 내리막길에서 브레이크를 세게 밟았더니 차가 끼익 소리를 냈어요.
examples.en: When I hit the brakes hard on the downhill road, the car let out a screech.

examples.ko: 낡은 문을 열 때마다 끼익 소리가 나요.
examples.en: The old door squeaks every time I open it.
The chair scraped back with a squeak.

examples.ko: 갑자기 자전거가 끼익 서서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A bicycle suddenly stopped with a screech and gave me a fright.

examples.ko: 문이 끼익 열리자 고양이가 살금살금 들어왔어요.
examples.en: As the door creaked open, a cat crept in.

explain: 타이어, 브레이크, 낡은 문, 의자처럼 딱딱한 것이 마찰할 때 나는 날카로운 소리예요. '끼이익'처럼 길게 늘이면 소리가 더 오래 나는 느낌이에요. 보통 '끼익 소리가 나다', '끼익 하고 서다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is the sharp sound hard things make when they rub together, like tires, brakes, an old door or a chair. Stretching it to '끼이익' makes the sound feel longer. It is usually used as '끼익 소리가 나다' (it makes a screech) or '끼익 하고 서다' (to stop with a screech).

examples.ko: 노천 온천에 몸을 담그고 멋진 풍경을 감상했어요.
examples.en: I soaked in an open-air hot spring and enjoyed the great view.

examples.ko: 노천에서 고기를 구워 먹으니 더 맛있었어요.
examples.en: Grilling and eating meat outdoors made it taste even better.

examples.ko: 이 시장은 지붕 없는 노천으로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This market is an open-air one with no roof.
I sat at an outdoor cafe and drank coffee.
The outdoor performance was canceled because of the rain.
The outdoor swimming pool closes in winter.

explain: 지붕이나 가림막 없이 하늘이 그대로 열린 곳을 말해서 '야외'와 비슷하지만, 보통 '노천 온천', '노천 카페'처럼 뒤에 장소를 붙여서 써요. 일상에서는 '야외', '밖'이 더 일반적이에요. 반대말은 '실내'예요.
explain_en: It means a place open to the sky with no roof or cover, so it is close to '야외' but usually appears before a place, as in '노천 온천' and '노천 카페'. In daily talk '야외' or '밖' is more general. The opposite is '실내' (indoors).

examples.en: An archipelago stretches across the sea off South Jeolla.
We took a boat and went sightseeing around the archipelago.
The sunset seen from the archipelago is really beautiful.

examples.ko: 다도해 해상 국립공원에 가 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever been to Dadohae Marine National Park?

examples.ko: 다도해 지역 사람들은 섬 사이를 배로 오가요.
examples.en: People in the archipelago region travel between islands by boat.

examples.ko: 여행 책에서 다도해의 풍경 사진을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw scenery photos of the archipelago in a travel book.

explain: 섬이 많이 모여 있는 바다를 말하는 일반 명사예요. 한국에서는 보통 전라남도 쪽 남서해안의 섬 지역을 떠올려요. 지명처럼 '다도해 해상 국립공원'으로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a general noun for a sea with many islands clustered together. In Korea it usually brings to mind the island region along the southwest coast near South Jeolla. It also appears in the park name '다도해 해상 국립공원'.

examples.en: On my trip to Europe, I visited a big cathedral.
The cathedral's ceiling is very high and ornate.
Seoul also has an old cathedral.

examples.ko: 대성당 앞 광장에서 사람들이 사진을 찍어요.
examples.en: People take photos in the square in front of the cathedral.

examples.ko: 이 대성당은 짓는 데 아주 오랜 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: This cathedral took a very long time to build.
On Sundays, Mass is held at the cathedral.

explain: '성당'은 천주교 교회를 가리키고, '대성당'은 그중 규모가 크고 웅장한 곳에 써요. 개신교 건물은 '교회'라고 불러요. 유럽 여행 이야기에서 특히 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '성당' refers to a Catholic church, and '대성당' is used for a large, grand one. Protestant buildings are called '교회'. It comes up especially when talking about trips to Europe.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 도로망이 잘 갖춰져 있어요.
examples.en: This city has a well-developed road network.

examples.ko: 새 도로망 덕분에 서울까지 한 시간이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the new road network, the trip to Seoul is an hour shorter.

examples.ko: 지방에도 고속도로 도로망을 더 늘려야 해요.
examples.en: We need to expand the highway network in the provinces too.
Island villages lack roads, so getting around is inconvenient.

examples.ko: 폭설 때문에 전국 도로망이 거의 막혔어요.
examples.en: Because of the heavy snow, the nationwide road network was almost blocked.
The road network is complicated, but I have a navigation app, so it's fine.

explain: '도로'는 길 하나하나이고, '도로망'은 그물처럼 이어진 길 전체를 말할 때 써요. 같은 '-망'이 붙은 '철도망, 통신망'도 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. 뉴스나 도시 계획 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '도로' is an individual road, while '도로망' refers to the whole web of connected roads. It helps to learn other '-망' words like '철도망' and '통신망'. It often appears in the news and in talk about city planning.

examples.en: There is a persimmon tree in the back of my grandmother's house.
We spread the peppers out to dry in the back yard.
The kids are playing hide-and-seek in the back yard.
If you go around to the back, you'll see a small vegetable garden.
The jar stand was usually at the back of the house.
I hung the blanket on the clothesline in the back yard.

explain: 집 뒤쪽의 마당이나 공간으로, 시골집이나 한옥 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 요즘 일상 대화에서는 '뒷마당'이 더 흔하고, 반대는 '앞마당'이에요.
explain_en: It means the yard or space behind a house, and often appears in stories about country homes or hanok. In everyday talk today '뒷마당' is more common, and the opposite is '앞마당'.

examples.en: The lighthouse light twinkles over the night sea.

examples.ko: 섬 끝에 하얀 등대가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A white lighthouse stands at the tip of the island.

examples.ko: 등대를 보고 배가 항구 쪽으로 방향을 잡았어요.
examples.en: The ship set its course toward the harbor by looking at the lighthouse.
The lighthouse keeper turns on the light every night.

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 저에게 인생의 등대 같은 분이에요.
examples.en: That teacher is like a lighthouse in my life.

examples.ko: 등대까지 걸어가는 데 삼십 분쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about thirty minutes to walk to the lighthouse.

explain: 배가 밤에 길을 찾도록 바닷가에 세우는 탑이에요. 비유로 길을 알려 주는 사람을 '등대 같은 사람'이라고 해요. 등대에서 일하는 사람은 '등대지기'예요.
explain_en: It is a tower built on the coast so ships can find their way at night. Figuratively, someone who shows you the way is called '등대 같은 사람'. A person who works at a lighthouse is a '등대지기'.

examples.en: The children played on a raft on the river.

examples.ko: 옛날 사람들은 나무로 뗏목을 만들어 강을 건넜어요.
examples.en: People long ago made rafts out of wood to cross rivers.
I went to Gangwon-do for a rafting experience.
A raft is drifting in from the sea.
In the movie the hero crosses the sea on a raft.
A raft is made by tying logs together.

explain: '뗏목'은 나무를 엮어 만든 것으로 사람이나 짐을 싣고 물 위를 가요. '배'와 달리 몸체가 따로 없고 통나무를 묶어서 만든 평평한 거예요. 공기를 넣은 고무 배는 '고무보트'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: '뗏목' is made of tied-together logs and carries people or goods on water. Unlike a '배', it has no hull; it is a flat platform of lashed logs. An inflatable rubber boat is called a '고무보트', which is a different thing.

examples.en: I only watched that person from a distance.

examples.ko: 아이는 먼발치에 서서 친구들이 노는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: The child stood a little way off and watched his friends play.
I can tell who it is just by glancing from afar.

examples.ko: 연예인을 먼발치에서나마 볼 수 있어서 기뻤어요.
examples.en: I was glad to see the celebrity, even if only from far away.

examples.ko: 사고 현장을 먼발치에서 구경하던 사람들이 모였어요.
examples.en: People who had been watching the scene of the accident from afar gathered.

examples.ko: 먼발치라도 좋으니 한번 만나 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: Even if it's only from afar, I want to see them once.

explain: '멀리서'보다 가까이 가지 못하고 떨어져서 보는 느낌이 있어요. 주로 '먼발치에서 보다/지켜보다/바라보다'처럼 써요. 마음은 가까이 가고 싶은데 거리를 두는 상황에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Compared with '멀리서', it carries the feel of being unable to get close and watching from a distance. It is mostly used as '먼발치에서 보다/지켜보다/바라보다'. It fits situations where you want to get closer but keep your distance.

examples.ko: 방파제 위에서 낚시를 하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people fish on top of the breakwater.

examples.ko: 파도가 높아서 방파제가 흔들리는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: The waves were so high that the breakwater seemed to shake.

examples.ko: 방파제를 따라 걸으면 바다 냄새가 나요.
examples.en: If you walk along the breakwater, you smell the sea.
There is a small lighthouse at the end of the breakwater.
The sound of waves crashing against the breakwater is refreshing.
A breakwater protects the harbor from waves.

explain: 항구나 바닷가에서 돌과 콘크리트를 길게 쌓아 놓은 곳이에요. 한국 사람들은 방파제 위에서 낚시하거나 산책하기도 해요. 비슷한 '제방'은 강이나 바다의 물이 넘치지 않게 쌓은 둑이에요.
explain_en: It is a long wall of stone and concrete at a harbor or the shore. Koreans also fish or take walks on top of a breakwater. The similar '제방' is an embankment built so the water of a river or sea doesn't overflow.

examples.en: I saw an old model of a sailing ship at the museum.
In the old days, people crossed the sea on sailing ships.
A sailing ship only moves forward when the wind blows.

examples.ko: 항구에 하얀 범선이 한 척 들어왔어요.
examples.en: A white sailing ship came into the harbor.

examples.ko: 범선에는 돛이 여러 개 달려 있어요.
examples.en: A sailing ship has several sails.
Most pirate ships in movies are sailing ships.

explain: 우리말로는 '돛단배'라고도 하는데, 범선은 큰 배를 말할 때 더 자연스러워요. 엔진으로 가는 배와 구별할 때도 써요. 배는 '한 척, 두 척'으로 세요.
explain_en: Native Korean also has '돛단배', but '범선' sounds more natural for a large ship. It is also used to set it apart from engine-powered ships. Ships are counted with '척', as in '한 척, 두 척'.

examples.en: During rush hour, the bus is packed.
The family lived crowded together in a small house.
I like the sound of my family bustling about in the kitchen.
The market alley was bustling with customers.
It's vacation, so the kids will be bustling around at home.
The cafe is so crowded that it's hard to study.

explain: 좁은 곳에 사람이 많이 모여 어수선하게 움직일 때 써요. '북적거리다'와 비슷하고, 일상에서는 '북적거리다'를 더 자주 써요. 불편하다는 뜻뿐 아니라 사람 사는 정겨운 느낌으로도 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when many people are packed into a small space and moving around in a busy way. It is similar to '북적거리다', which is more common in daily speech. It can sound uncomfortable, but also warm, like lively family life.

examples.en: The ship arrived at the dock.
They sell fish cheaply at the pier.
A truck loaded with cargo drove onto the wharf.
In the evening I took a walk along the pier.
The piers in this city are crowded with tourists.

examples.ko: 부두 근처에 맛있는 해산물 식당이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a good seafood restaurant near the dock.

explain: '부두'는 배를 대고 사람이 타고 내리거나 짐을 싣고 내리는 구체적인 자리예요. '항구'는 배가 드나드는 도시나 지역 전체의 느낌이고, '부두'는 그 안에서 배를 대는 곳이에요.
explain_en: '부두' is the specific spot where ships tie up and people or cargo get on and off. '항구' is the whole harbor town or area, and a '부두' is one of the places inside it.

examples.en: A huge airship is floating in the sky.
In the old days, airships also carried people.
An airship is much slower than an airplane.

examples.ko: 저는 비행선을 타고 여행하는 상상을 해요.
examples.en: I imagine traveling by airship.
The airship ad stood out in the sky.

examples.ko: 만화 속 비행선이 너무 멋있어서 따라 그렸어요.
examples.en: The airship in the cartoon was so cool that I drew it too.

explain: 비행선은 가벼운 기체를 채운 큰 풍선 같은 몸체로 하늘을 나는 탈것이에요. 날개로 나는 '비행기'와 달라서 아주 천천히 움직여요. 요즘에는 타는 일보다 광고나 영화에서 더 자주 봐요.
explain_en: 비행선 is a vehicle with a big balloon-like body filled with lighter-than-air gas. It is different from a 비행기, which flies on wings, and it moves very slowly. These days you see it more in ads and movies than you actually ride one.

examples.en: There are many mountains in the northwest of Seoul.

examples.ko: 오늘은 서북 지방에 비가 올 거예요.
examples.en: Rain will fall in the northwest region today.
The wind blew from the northwest, so it was cold.

examples.ko: 서북 방향으로 이십 분쯤 걸으면 역이 나와요.
examples.en: If you walk northwest for about twenty minutes, you reach the station.

examples.ko: 지도에서 서북 쪽 끝에 있는 섬을 찾았어요.
examples.en: I found the island at the northwest end of the map.
The northwest area has long winters.

explain: 서쪽과 북쪽 사이의 방향이에요. 같은 방향을 '북서'라고도 해요. 다른 방향도 '동북', '동남', '서남'처럼 말하거나 '북동', '남동', '남서'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is the direction between west and north. The same direction is also called 북서. The other directions work the same way: 동북, 동남, 서남 or 북동, 남동, 남서.

examples.ko: 배에 타서 먼저 제 선실을 찾았어요.
examples.en: After boarding the ship, I first looked for my cabin.
The cabin was small, so it was awkward to put my luggage down.

examples.ko: 파도가 심해서 하루 종일 선실에 누워 있었어요.
examples.en: The waves were rough, so I lay in my cabin all day.
Our family booked a cabin for four.
I liked that I could see the sea from the cabin window.
I came out of the cabin and went up to the deck.

explain: 배 안에서 승객이나 선원이 지내는 방이라서, 여객선이나 크루즈 이야기에 나와요. 비행기 안은 '기내'라고 하고 '선실'은 배에만 써요.
explain_en: It is the room where passengers or crew stay on a ship, so it appears when talking about ferries and cruises. Inside a plane people say '기내', and '선실' is used only for ships.

examples.en: In a monastery, people live quietly and pray.
There is an old monastery in the mountains.
During my trip I toured a monastery in Europe.

examples.ko: 수도원 안에서는 큰 소리로 말하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not speak loudly inside the monastery.
A friend who entered a monastery sent a letter.

examples.ko: 그 수도원은 직접 만든 빵으로 유명해요.
examples.en: That monastery is famous for its homemade bread.

explain: '수도원'은 기독교 수도자가 모여 사는 곳이에요. 여자 수도자만 사는 곳은 '수녀원'이라고 따로 불러요. 불교의 절은 '절'이나 '사찰'이라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: 수도원 is where Christian monks or nuns live together. A place with only women is called 수녀원 separately. A Buddhist temple is 절 or 사찰, so those are kept apart.

examples.en: A motorcycle whizzed past me.

examples.ko: 찬 바람이 쌩 불어서 코트 깃을 세웠어요.
examples.en: A cold wind whistled by, so I turned up my coat collar.

examples.ko: 차들이 쌩 달리는 도로라서 건널 때 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: Cars speed along this road, so you have to be careful when crossing.
The child dashed off in a flash.

examples.ko: 열차가 쌩 하는 소리를 내며 역을 지나가요.
examples.en: The train goes through the station with a whooshing sound.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 인사도 받지 않고 쌩 가 버렸어요.
examples.en: My friend didn't even return my greeting and just rushed off.

explain: 바람이 차갑게 불거나 무언가가 빠르게 스쳐 지나갈 때의 소리와 모습을 나타내요. 계속 빠르게 달리거나 바람이 세게 불 때는 '쌩쌩'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It expresses the sound and look of a cold wind blowing or something passing by quickly. When something keeps running fast or the wind blows hard continuously, people say '쌩쌩'.

examples.en: There is a grain of rice around your mouth.

examples.ko: 해 질 무렵 마을 언저리까지 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: At sunset, I walked to the edge of the village.

examples.ko: 기억 언저리에서 맴돌 뿐 이름이 생각 안 나요.
examples.en: It's just circling at the edge of my memory, and I can't recall the name.

examples.ko: 눈 언저리가 빨개진 걸 보니 울었나 봐요.
examples.en: The area around your eyes is red, so you must have been crying.

examples.ko: 우리가 아는 건 진실의 언저리일 뿐이에요.
examples.en: What we know is only the fringe of the truth.
Many people get married around thirty.

explain: '가장자리'가 물건의 끝을 말한다면, '언저리'는 그 끝 주변까지 넓게 가리켜요. 입 언저리, 눈 언저리처럼 몸에도 쓰고, '서른 언저리'처럼 나이나 시기를 어림잡을 때도 써요.
explain_en: While '가장자리' points to the very edge of an object, '언저리' covers the area around that edge. It is used for the body, as in 입 언저리 (around the mouth), and also to estimate an age or time, as in '서른 언저리' (around thirty).

examples.ko: 마을 언덕 위에 작은 예배당이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small chapel on top of the village hill.
I go to church with my family every Sunday.
It was quiet and warm inside the chapel.

examples.ko: 그 예배당은 백 년 넘게 마을 사람들이 찾아오는 곳이에요.
examples.en: That chapel is a place villagers have visited for over a hundred years.

examples.ko: 결혼식은 학교 안 예배당에서 하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to hold the wedding in the chapel on the school grounds.
They started fundraising to build a new chapel.

explain: 예배를 드리는 건물 자체를 가리켜요. 일상에서 사람들이 가는 곳은 보통 '교회'라고 하고, '예배당'은 건물이나 학교·병원 안의 작은 공간을 말할 때 자주 써요. 천주교는 '성당', 불교는 '절'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the building where worship takes place. In daily life people usually say '교회' for where they go, while '예배당' is often used for the building itself or a small space inside a school or hospital. Catholics say '성당' and Buddhists say '절'.

examples.ko: 그분은 끝내 고국에 돌아오지 못하고 이국땅에 묻혔어요.
examples.en: He never made it back to his homeland and was buried in a foreign land.

examples.ko: 이국땅에서 혼자 살다 보니 가족이 정말 그리워요.
examples.en: Living alone in a foreign land, I really miss my family.
My first Lunar New Year in a foreign land was lonely.

examples.ko: 말이 안 통하는 이국땅에서 길을 잃어 당황했어요.
examples.en: I got lost in a foreign land where I couldn't speak the language, and I panicked.
I saw off my friend at the airport as he left for a foreign land.

examples.ko: 이국땅에서도 한국 음식을 먹으면 힘이 나요.
examples.en: Even in a foreign land, eating Korean food gives me energy.

explain: '외국'보다 쓸쓸함이나 그리움 같은 감정이 담겨요. 고향을 떠나 사는 사람의 이야기에서 자주 나오고, 짝이 되는 말은 '고국'이나 '고향'이에요. 단순히 외국 여행을 말할 때는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '외국' (foreign country), it carries feelings like loneliness and longing. It often appears in stories about people living away from home, and its counterparts are '고국' and '고향'. It's not used for simply talking about traveling abroad.

examples.en: Many relatives gathered at my grandmother's funeral home.
I prepared condolence money before going to the funeral home.
There is a funeral home next to the hospital.
I met my cousin at the funeral home after a long time.
It took thirty minutes by taxi to get to the funeral home.
A funeral home is a place where you need to be quiet.

explain: 한국 장례식장은 보통 병원 안이나 옆에 있어서 '병원 장례식장'이라고도 해요. 가면 검은색이나 어두운 옷을 입고 '조의금'을 내고 조문하는 게 일반적이에요. 인사는 '삼가 고인의 명복을 빕니다'처럼 정중하게 해요.
explain_en: Funeral homes in Korea are usually inside or next to a hospital, so people also say '병원 장례식장'. Visitors normally wear black or dark clothes, give '조의금' and pay their respects. The greeting is polite, like '삼가 고인의 명복을 빕니다'.

examples.en: This bus's final stop is Seoul Station.
Please wake me when we reach the last stop.

examples.ko: 여행의 종착지가 어디인지 아직 정하지 못했어요.
examples.en: I haven't decided where the trip will end yet.
The train has almost reached its final stop.

examples.ko: 인생의 종착지가 어디일지 가끔 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Sometimes I wonder where life's final destination will be.

examples.ko: 이 지하철은 종착지까지 한 시간 넘게 걸려요.
examples.en: This subway takes over an hour to reach the last stop.

explain: 버스나 지하철에서는 '종점', '종착역'이라는 말을 더 많이 써요. '종착지'는 긴 여행이나 인생의 마지막 목적지처럼 비유로도 쓰기 좋아요. 반대말은 '출발지'예요.
explain_en: For buses and subways, '종점' and '종착역' are more common. '종착지' also works well as a metaphor for the end of a long journey or of life. Its opposite is '출발지' (starting point).

examples.en: There is a big plaza in the central part of the city.

examples.ko: 이 지도에서 중앙부는 빨간색으로 표시돼 있어요.
examples.en: On this map, the central area is marked in red.
The seats in the middle section of the hall are the most expensive.
The central part of the island is made up of mountains.

examples.ko: 다리 중앙부가 약해서 공사를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The middle of the bridge is weak, so they are doing repairs.
It plays when you press the middle of the screen.

explain: 중앙부는 '가운데'와 비슷하지만 설명문과 지도, 기사에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서는 '가운데'나 '한가운데'라고 해요. 같은 식으로 '북부', '남부'처럼 '-부'가 붙으면 어떤 지역의 한 부분을 가리켜요.
explain_en: 중앙부 is close to '가운데' but is a stiff word used in explanations, maps and articles. In daily life people say '가운데' or '한가운데'. In the same way, '-부' in '북부' and '남부' marks one part of an area.

examples.en: The plane landed safely at Incheon Airport.
We are landing soon, so please fasten your seat belt.

examples.ko: 눈이 많이 와서 착륙할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: It snowed a lot, so the plane could not land.
I saw a photo of the spacecraft that landed on the moon.
The moment it landed, the passengers clapped.

examples.ko: 안개 때문에 다른 공항에 착륙해서 많이 늦었어요.
examples.en: We landed at a different airport because of fog, so we were very late.

explain: 반대말은 '이륙하다'예요. 사람이 비행기에서 나올 때는 '내리다'를 쓰고, 비행기가 땅에 닿을 때는 '착륙하다'를 써요. 우주선과 헬리콥터에도 쓰고, 'ㄱ'과 'ㄹ'이 만나는 소리 변화 때문에 '창뉴카다'로 발음해요.
explain_en: The opposite is 이륙하다. A person getting off a plane uses 내리다, while the plane touching the ground is 착륙하다. It also works for spacecraft and helicopters, and a sound change (ㄱ+ㄹ becomes ㅇ+ㄴ, and ㄱ+ㅎ becomes ㅋ) makes it pronounced 창뉴카다.

examples.en: On the weekend, I went to an observatory with my family.

examples.ko: 큰 망원경이 있는 천문대로 소풍을 갔어요.
examples.en: We went on a trip to an observatory with a big telescope.

examples.ko: 산 위 천문대는 별이 잘 보여서 인기예요.
examples.en: The observatory on the mountain is popular because the stars are clear.
An observatory staff member explained the constellations.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 천문대에서 일하고 싶었어요.
examples.en: I have wanted to work at an observatory since I was little.
When the observatory roof opens, you can see the sky.

explain: '과학관'은 전시를 보는 곳이고 '천문대'는 망원경으로 실제 하늘을 보는 곳이에요. 비슷한 말로 '관측소'가 있지만 일상에서는 '천문대'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '천문대에 가다', '천문대를 견학하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: A '과학관' is a place to see exhibits, while a '천문대' is where you view the real sky through a telescope. A similar word is '관측소', but in daily life '천문대' is far more common. People say '천문대에 가다' or '천문대를 견학하다'.

examples.en: Every evening I take a walk along the stream.
The cherry blossoms bloomed by the stream, so it was crowded.

examples.ko: 우리 집은 천변 쪽이라서 아침에 새소리가 들려요.
examples.en: My house is on the stream side, so I hear birds in the morning.

examples.ko: 천변 자전거 길에서는 속도를 줄여 주세요.
examples.en: Please slow down on the bike path by the stream.
Kids are playing and catching fish by the stream.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 천변 길을 통제해요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, they close off the road by the stream.

explain: '강변'이 큰 강가라면 '천변'은 작은 하천의 가장자리를 말해요. '○○천변'처럼 하천 이름 뒤에 붙여서도 써요. 산책길이나 자전거 길과 같이 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: While '강변' is the bank of a big river, '천변' is the edge of a smaller stream. It can also be attached after a stream's name, like '○○천변'. It is often mentioned with walking paths and bike paths.

examples.ko: 산 위에 높은 철탑이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A tall steel tower stands on top of the mountain.

examples.ko: 철탑 위에서 작업하는 분들이 대단해 보여요.
examples.en: The people who work on top of the pylon look amazing.

examples.ko: 철탑을 따라 전깃줄이 길게 이어져 있어요.
examples.en: Power lines stretch long along the pylons.
I can see pylons lined up in the distance.
A bird built a nest on the tall steel tower.

examples.ko: 논 가운데 철탑 몇 개가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A few steel towers stand in the middle of the rice fields.

explain: 쇠 구조물로 만든 높은 탑이에요. 전깃줄을 걸어 놓은 송전 철탑을 가리킬 때가 많아요. 관광용 탑은 보통 '타워'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is a tall tower built from a steel structure, and often means a power transmission pylon holding up electric lines. Sightseeing towers are usually just called '타워'.

examples.ko: 국경 초소에서 군인이 경계를 서고 있어요.
examples.en: A soldier is standing guard at the border post.
There is a small guard post at the entrance of the mountain path.

examples.ko: 초소 앞에서 신분증을 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to show your ID in front of the checkpoint.

examples.ko: 아파트 입구 초소에 경비 아저씨가 계세요.
examples.en: A security guard is at the booth at the apartment entrance.

examples.ko: 초소 근무를 서는 병사가 밤새 깨어 있었어요.
examples.en: The soldier on guard duty stayed awake all night.

examples.ko: 낡은 초소는 이제 전망대로 쓰이고 있어요.
examples.en: The old guard post is now used as an observation deck.

explain: 군대나 경찰, 경비가 지키며 서는 작은 건물이나 장소예요. 아파트의 작은 방은 보통 '경비실'이라고 해요. '초소형 사이즈'의 초소는 한자가 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a small building or place where the military, police or guards keep watch. At apartment buildings, the small guard room is usually called '경비실'. The 초소 in '초소형 사이즈' (ultra-small size) is a different word with different Chinese characters.

examples.ko: 아들이 최전방 부대에서 군 복무를 해요.
examples.en: My son is serving in the army at a front-line unit.
A long fence stretches along the front line.
Medical staff worked on the front line of the response to the infectious disease.

examples.ko: 그는 판매 현장의 최전방에 서서 고객을 만나요.
examples.en: He stands at the front line of sales and meets customers.
It is hard for ordinary people to enter the front-line area.

examples.ko: 감독은 가장 빠른 선수를 최전방으로 올려 보냈어요.
examples.en: The coach sent his fastest player up to the front.

explain: 원래는 군대에서 적과 가장 가까운 곳을 가리키지만, 요즘은 '가장 앞에서 직접 부딪히는 자리'를 비유할 때도 써요. '전방'은 앞쪽 전체이고 '최전방'은 그중 맨 앞이에요. '최'가 '가장'의 뜻을 더해 줘요.

phrases.en: to work on the front line
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대가 아니어도 위험하거나 힘든 현장에서 가장 먼저 직접 일하는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not only military: used for people doing the hardest, most direct work in a tough field.

explain_en: Originally 최전방 means the place in the military closest to the enemy, but now it is also used figuratively for the spot that faces problems head-on. 전방 is the whole forward area, and 최전방 is the very front of it. The 최 adds the sense of 'most'.

examples.en: The ship's departure was canceled because of the typhoon.
The departure time is nine in the morning.
The fog was thick, so they postponed the departure by a day.

examples.ko: 오늘 출항은 바람이 강해서 어려울 것 같아요.
examples.en: Setting sail today seems difficult because the wind is strong.

examples.ko: 첫 출항 때 느낀 설렘을 아직도 잊지 못해요.
examples.en: I still can't forget the excitement I felt on my first voyage out.

examples.ko: 출항 전에 안전 점검을 꼭 해야 해요.
examples.en: You must do a safety check before setting sail.

explain: 배가 항구를 떠날 때 쓰는 말이라 일반적인 '출발'과 달라요. 반대말은 '입항'이고, 날씨 때문에 배가 못 뜰 때 '출항 금지', '출항 취소'라는 말이 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when a ship leaves port, so it differs from the general word '출발' (departure). Its opposite is '입항', and phrases like '출항 금지' and '출항 취소' often appear in the news when weather keeps ships in.

examples.en: Small fishing boats came into the harbor.
On the weekend I visited a small harbor on the West Sea.
I ate raw fish at a restaurant near the harbor.

examples.ko: 이 포구는 해 질 무렵이 제일 예뻐요.
examples.en: This harbor is prettiest around sunset.
The fishermen left the harbor at dawn.
The harbor village has many quiet alleys.

explain: '항구'보다 작고 정겨운 바닷가 마을 느낌이 있어요. 큰 배가 오가는 곳은 '항구', 어선이 드나드는 작은 곳은 '포구'라고 해요. 여행 글에서 '포구 마을'이라는 말을 자주 봐요.
explain_en: Compared with 항구, 포구 feels smaller and more homey. A big ship port is a 항구, while a small place for fishing boats is a 포구. In travel writing you often see the phrase 포구 마을.
